recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. I have used their teas and tinctures on an almost daily basis for years now. Kyle is a great friend of InnerVerse and has appeared on the channel more times than I can count. These products work, not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Name: Tippecanoe Herbs
recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Offer Line: Use coupon code "innerverse" at checkout for a 10% discount!

recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.
recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Name: The Sonic Slider

recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Body: LotusWei provides amazing and transformative plant essence elixirs, using one of nature's most gentle and beautiful elements: the flowers themselves. Led by founder Katie Hess, LotusWei supports customers with diverse products that operate on homeopathic principles and energetic resonances. I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. In other words, LotusWei Elixirs help me be a better podcaster and Biofield Tuner. Benefits accumulate over long term use!
recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Name: LotusWei Flower Elixirs
recFdBmTf1pJJOP6S.Offer Line: Use my affiliate link to support InnerVerse

recIZOksQw0qqj7L0.Body: George Wiseman is the inventor of the AquaCure AC50 and founder of Eagle Research, where he has spent decades developing hydrogen and oxygen (Brown's gas) technology for health and home use. He has appeared on InnerVerse multiple times to talk about hydrogen as a macronutrient and EZ water.
recIZOksQw0qqj7L0.Name: AquaCure AC50
recIZOksQw0qqj7L0.Offer Line: Use coupon code "innerverse" for a discount

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.
recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Name: Clive de Carle

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

recLy5DrjiTT1fS5p.Bio: Benjamin Balderson is a practicing alchemist who has taught laboratory (practical) alchemy on InnerVerse, covering distillation, alcohol-free tinctures, and the alchemical patterns found in nature; he shares his work under the banner "Odin's Alchemy."
recLy5DrjiTT1fS5p.Name: Benjamin Balderson

recZWht3G3mnVowV0.Bio: Matt Powers, known as "The Permaculture Student," is a citizen scientist and permaculture educator focused on soil health, composting, and sustainable growing methods.
recZWht3G3mnVowV0.Name: Matt Powers

recikO1LzuvqEbe0G.Bio: James Frosch is the founder of Family Fungi, a holistic wellness homestead providing mushroom-based medicines and DIY mycology wisdom, discussed on InnerVerse alongside topics like enzyme function and endocrine health.
recikO1LzuvqEbe0G.Name: James Frosch

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Microbes as Shapeshifting Soil Builders", "body": "Chance opened by questioning linear evolution in favor of cyclical rebirth shaped by conditions. Matt answered with a desert restoration story, saying mushrooms appeared in a Saudi Arabian landscape after rock dams and trees returned water to the land. He argued that unclassified DNA fragments in organic matter were eaten and expressed by microbes through horizontal gene transfer, so microbes recoded each other and changed species quickly. Matt added that this made microbes the engine of adaptation in soil, compost and the human body."}, {"title": "Soil Myths and the Alchemical Great Work", "body": "Benjamin described a heathen story in which Lif and Lifthrasir were hidden in mud by Odin and mankind returned from them after Ragnarok. Chance framed the evening as a meeting of the scientist and the wizard, bringing together science, myth and other cosmologies. Later in the show, one guest described the alchemical great work as sulfur passing through mercury to enliven salt and said he built faith by watching it happen again and again in the lab."}, {"title": "The Living Soil as a Battery", "body": "Matt argued that plants worked like solar panels, splitting water and storing protons in organic matter, so rich soils acted as batteries. He said tillage and mining removed nutrient charges from the ground. Another guest compared the world to a biochemical battery that sulfated over time and read Ragnarok as a hard electrical charge that cleared the buildup. A later speaker tied the start of tillage to the Adam and Eve story and said permaculture tried to reconcile that break with nature."}, {"title": "Culture Vessels, Consortia, and Gut Health", "body": "James Frosch joined from Family Fungi and argued that human bodies were culture vessels, so what people fed themselves shaped what expressed outwardly. He said healing the soul meant healing the soil and the gut. When Michelle asked about fertilizing with hot spring water, the panel urged testing and a small trial. Matt explained how to collect indigenous microorganisms from the spring, dry ground, sun and shade, then combine them into a library for a whole property."}, {"title": "Placenta, Mushrooms, and Synchronicity", "body": "A guest asked Gabe about placenta eating, and Gabe linked the Phrygian cap, the red cap of the mushroom and the placental cap into one initiation motif. Gabe also described Tibetan and Catholic lore about unusual births and called communication the primary nature of nature. In the closing round Gabe told of finding a huge mushroom beside his head two days after hearing about one said to attract mysterious light, and not recognizing the match until a month later. Chance closed by thanking the guests and promising links to everyone, including Family Fungi, in the description."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Matt Powers and Benjamin Balderson join us to discuss the possibility that permaculture is more than just a gardening technique. Does the living soil contain the record of all life, and have the ability to generate complex beings to populate environments with the appropriate organisms? Heathen cosmology may have been more literal than we thought…
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "Because I'm starting to really see the picture of the possibility that life and location and everything is like frequency based and the conditions energetically of an environment determine what you find there, not the record that we consider to be linear.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "And I really wanted to bring together the mind of the scientist and the wizard, and the heathen, and what other cosmologies we might bring to the table here.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/a784fd99-3e6f-436c-a8f3-c4f913b855ed/profile-pic.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "So let's start in Saudi Arabia, let's start in the desert, let's start in an area where in living memory, no one's seen a mushroom growing out of the ground.", "author": "Matt Powers", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/bf13fb2e-84a5-4fd6-a8ca-b479d3dd23aa/MATT-POWERS.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "But the reality now we understand through horizontal gene transfer is that microbes eat the dead DNA around them consuming in the organic matter.
